notes.title: LaserZone is now released on Steam!
notes.content:
[h1]Greetings[/h1]

Hello, everyone! 
I am Jung Hwan Hwang – the level designer behind LaserZone. 
I’m speaking on behalf of our team and our director since I am the only person who can write in English.

[h1]What We've Been Up to[/h1]

As you guessed, LaserZone has been finally released! Our team is excited and extremely happy at the moment.
It took more than 3 years to release our game, and there had been tough problems lurking around the corners. The first two years were slow-going since we lacked manpower. In addition, there were conflicts between crew members, COVID-19 prevented offline meetings, and our rating got rejected once. A handful of reasons delayed the release, and it hit our team’s morale even though no one said anything about it.

However, our director aims to complete any product no matter what. His tenacity gave us the motivation to stay cool and deliver a polished game to the market.
7 months have passed since the initial release date. However, having tested our game 7 months before and now, I’m glad we didn’t rush our release.

[h1]Q&A[/h1]

In the last news, we promised you to give extra information about the game on the release date. 
We would like to clear out some of the questions you got by preparing a Q&A. I wrote down 4 answers for 4 corresponding questions.
This section excludes any information that is already on the Store Page.
 
Q. How much content is in the game? How long is the playtime?

A. There are a total of [u]160 maps[/u] available, split into 6 Chapters.
132 maps are designed to deliver the puzzle-solving experience. 39 maps out of the 132 serve as tutorials. They teach you how to use, exploit, and combine newly introduced game mechanics.
On the other hand, you can take a rest in the other 28 maps. They offer free resources for upgrades and often include cinematic events for advancing the story. 
Based on the FGT reports we’ve collected, it will approximately take [u]7~9 hours[/u] to finish the game. But please note that playtime may vary between players.

Q. How difficult is the game?

A. Our game targets [u]casual-to-mid core[/u] players.
Based on a scale of 1 to 10, the average difficulty for Chapters starts at 2, and gradually increases up to 6. 
However, there are some difficulty spikes to keep good players interested. Some maps require faster reflexes than others too.
But after you overcome them, difficulty settles down for a short time.
You can easily complete Chapters 1 and 2, but you will need to start paying some attention from there.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/8f4a94a3322b505027cd3055a9a896e4429e54ac.jpg[/img]


Q. Please tell us about Configuration options.

A. LaserZone supports resolution options up to 2560x1440(QHD) and custom key-bindings. Controller support is NOT in the game. Texture options are NOT provided because the game does not require high-end PCs, and CPU is more important than GPU (for playing this game). 

Q. Will there be any future support from the development team?
A. We are planning to add [u]Steam Achievements[/u]. We will attempt to [u]fix any unexpected bugs[/u] by receiving reports from players on the Steam Forum too.
But please note that the official release version for LaserZone is meant to be [u]a complete experience, a finished product[/u]. 
While we don’t have any concrete plans at the moment, we will consider adding new features and content if a suggestion receives a certain degree of popularity.

[h1]Signing Off[/h1]

I hope that answers your questions!
Again, thank you very much for checking out LaserZone! 
And if you decided to get the game, we hope you enjoy it!

notes.title: Dev Log #3
notes.content:
Hello, everyone. I’m the level designer of the LaserZone. I hope you are having a good day.

It’s been 3 weeks since we posted the announcement about delaying the game’s release. As promised back then, I’m here to relay information about what’s going on in our project before June arrives.


[h1]Game, Ready for Testing[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/5cb8fcd7e9a5332d5e4b3d0cde343e3534663bf8.png[/img]
[i]Our project build folder, including the working .exe file.[/i]

Let’s cut to the chase.
We’ve completed a game version for the upcoming second Focus Group Test (or FGT). 
This version is [b]intended to become the release version[/b] if we don’t receive critical feedback during the second FGT.

That’s basically the gist of this Dev Log. But if you want more details, please continue reading.


[h1]A 3-Week Schedule for Improving the Game[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/489e65882a92302318557fb73c18a81347a4ff3e.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37670370/0441ca66a5c3111d4b418ad94c0d3d7224cdc38f.png[/img]
[i]We’ve been using a new project-management program called “Monday”.[/i]

After the first FGT, these are the four main goals we’ve been attempting to accomplish:

[b][olist]
[*] Reducing action/control difficulty in Chapter 4~6
[*] Getting rid of as many bugs as possible
[*] Improving controllability for UI and in-game actions
[*] Implementing a feature that teaches new mechanics for players
[/olist][/b]

We also wanted to address relatively less-urgent tasks such as improving animations, refining English translations, and sound design within the milestone.

Monday tells us our completion rate for the latest version is at [b]95.9%[/b]. 94 out of 98 tasks have been done, and the rest is something that we couldn’t wrap up in time. 
Fortunately, those tasks aren’t critical enough to delay the game’s release (again). We’ll take a look at them after the test is done. 

Right now, we are ready to start the second FGT which will take around 2~3 days. For this FGT, our biggest interest is to receive reports of technical errors that were somehow overlooked during the last 3 weeks of development.

Other members have tested new features, and I did play the game from start to finish. We found and corrected the last critical bug two days ago, so we are expecting the game to fully function.
We’ll also ask our testers if the aforementioned 4 goals have been met.


[h1]Closing[/h1]

If the general consensus from our testers is positive, then we will hire an outsource for a new trailer, and ship the game once we receive the video.

That’s it for today!
I’ll return when we decided what to do after the second FGT.
Thank you for reading, and stay healthy in this global pandemic.

Signing off,
Jung Hwan Hwang
